claims.text: Point Roberts is a pene-exclave of the US state of Washington on the southernmost tip of the Tsawwassen peninsula, south of Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada.
The area had a population of 1,191 at the 2020 census.
It is reached from the rest of the United States by travelling 25 mi (40 km) through Canada, or without passing through Canada by boat or private airplane.

Point Roberts was created when the United Kingdom and the United States settled the Pacific Northwest border dispute with the Oregon Treaty (concluded 15 June 1846): the two parties agreed that the 49th parallel would define the boundary, and the small area that incorporates Point Roberts is south of it.

The 49th parallel was accepted as the boundary without precise knowledge of its effects; later, as the Boundary Commission surveyed the line, the British government realised the peninsula of Point Roberts would be an isolated part of the United States.

The British Foreign Office instructed its Boundary Commissioner to ask that Point Roberts be left to Britain; it is not known how the US commissioner responded, but Point Roberts remained part of the United States.
The Canadian border was closed to non-essential travel in March 2020 and fully reopened in August 2021.
In 2020 a study found that Point Roberts had lost 80 percent of its business and hundreds of seasonal residents as a result of the pandemic and border shutdown.
